summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis and recent Puestow procedure was readmitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He reported a syncopal episode possibly related to pain, initially concerning for seizure but determined to be a pseudoseizure. CT imaging showed expected post-surgical changes without abscess, mild colonic wall thickening of uncertain significance, and a trace pericardial effusion. He was managed medically with IV pain control and antiemetics, advanced to a regular diet, and remained stable. Wound cultures grew Staphylococcus aureus and Group B Streptococcus, interpreted as skin flora without evidence of infection. He improved clinically and was discharged home with oral pain medication and follow-up plans. No surgical intervention was required.
